steps.code:
# Parse the note content to extract songs with TODO release dates
import re

content = note['content']
lines = content.split('\n')
songs = []
for line in lines:
    if line.startswith('- '):
        # Extract title, artists, release
        m = re.match(r'- (.+?) BY (.+?) RELEASED_AT (.+)$', line)
        if m:
            title = m.group(1).strip()
            artists_str = m.group(2).strip()
            release = m.group(3).strip()
            artists = [a.strip() for a in artists_str.split(',')]
            songs.append({'title': title, 'artists': artists, 'release': release, 'line': line})
        else:
            print("Could not parse line:", line)

# Show songs with TODO
todo_songs = [s for s in songs if s['release'] == 'TODO']
print(f"Found {len(todo_songs)} songs with TODO")
for s in todo_songs:
    print(s['title'], '|', s['artists'])

# Now let's update the note content with the release month/year for each TODO song
import re
from datetime import datetime

# Build a mapping from song title to release date
# We already have release_dates dict

# Parse the current content lines
new_lines = []
for line in content.split('\n'):
    if 'RELEASED_AT TODO' in line:
        # Extract song title: line format "- <title> BY <artists> RELEASED_AT TODO"
        # Use regex to get title
        m = re.match(r'- (.+?) BY .+ RELEASED_AT TODO', line)
        if m:
            title = m.group(1)
            release_date = release_dates.get(title)
            if release_date:
                # Convert to month/year format
                dt = datetime.fromisoformat(release_date)
                month_year = f"{dt.month:02d}/{dt.year}"
                # Replace TODO with month/year
                new_line = line.replace('RELEASED_AT TODO', f'RELEASED_AT {month_year}')
                new_lines.append(new_line)
            else:
                print(f"Missing release date for {title}")
                new_lines.append(line)  # keep as is
        else:
            new_lines.append(line)
    else:
        new_lines.append(line)

new_content = '\n'.join(new_lines)
print(new_content)
